adversarial_review: The three-class taxonomy and claims that members trade identically are broad untested assertions; fundamental and speculative forces coexist. Aggregation does not preclude persistent trends, and ETF applicability cannot be inferred from an old futures opinion. The dated minimum-capital and software-platform claims are not current specifications. The coffee counterfactual assumes fills, sizing and exit history despite admitted capacity concerns; the displayed chart exits after 65 bars, so it is not an independently specified original-rule result. Its initial stop differs from twice the prose N and equal profit per pyramided contract is an approximation. The combined long/short RAR exceeds either component without a clear shared capital normalization; do not read this as a free diversification gain. More systems bring operational costs and can all fail together. Source dating of the famous gold/silver peak is unverified and not accepted as a trading input. Ecological analogies do not prove that every simple strategy is robust.

A graph capped at 100% does not show potential deficits beyond starting capital. Claimed savings of more than 100 million and the claim that later signals lose more are unverified counterfactuals. Source unit limits are historical system parameters, not approved risk limits for this project. Low volatility can invite excessive notional size unless a separate cap exists. Anecdotes about doctors and dentists do not establish occupational causes of trading failure. Risk preferences are individual, but calculation errors and ignoring liabilities remain objectively testable mistakes.
